title: Package
description: A file with transliteration rules and related data

id.description: A unique ID for this package. Data inside this package which can be referenced will be namespaced to this ID. For example, a unicode block group with ID 'latin-letters' in a package with ID 'builtin' can be referenced via the string 'builtin:latin-letters

name.description: A user-friendly name for this package

description.description: An optional description of the contents of the package, for users

blockGroups.description: Groups of Unicode blocks (or subsets of blocks) to be referenced by rules, to know whether an input with no matches should be treated as a warning

name.description: A user-friendly name for this block group (e.g. 'Latin letters')

note.description: A note, usually denoting the purpose of this block group

items.description: A Unicode block (or subset of a block) which contains ranges of code points

name.description: A user-friendly name for this block (e.g. 'Latin Extended-C'). Should match the actual Unicode block name, but doesn't have to. You could technically have a single big block with all the code point ranges, but this is discouraged, as it makes it hard for the user to know which Unicode blocks are used

ranges.description: The numeric ranges of all code points used in this block. You can have an empty ranges list to denote that a block was considered, but had nothing related to what this block group wanted (e.g. a Latin block only had modifier code points, but this block group wants letters)

items.description: The inclusive start of the code point range. For example, ASCII 'A' would be 65
The inclusive end of the code point range. For example, ASCII 'Z' would be 90

rules.description: Rules that transform a sequence of code points. Both inputs and rules are normalized to NFD form, which means that letters with an accent will be transformed, even if your rule only has a rule for a letter without an accent

name.description: A user-friendly name for these transliteration rules (e.g. 'Non-standard Latin to Russian Cyrillic')

description.description: An optional description of the transliteration rules. Should contain the purpose of the rules and a source if this is an existing scheme

map.description: The actual transliteration table/map. Case-insensitive, but usually lowercase. Supports arbitrary code point sequences

items.description: The case-insensitive input code point sequence (e.g. 'shch')
The case-insensitive output code point sequence (e.g. 'щ'). Can be an empty string (e.g. you want to eliminate soft signs, so you map 'ь' to nothing)

inBlockGroups.description: A list of block groups that these rules expect as the input. If an input sequence has a code point in this group, but doesn't map to anything, then a warning is shown, as this usually indicates a typo. Can be empty if you don't want these rules to generate these types of warnings, although this isn't recommended. Should be generous but not all-encompassing (e.g. rules which transliterate Latin to Cyrillic should use a group with all the Latin letters as the input, but not numbers, modifiers, symbols, etc...)

items.description: A namespaced ID pointing to a block group (e.g. 'builtin:latin-letters')

outBlockGroups.description: Same as inBlockGroups, but for outputs. This might seem useless, as warnings are generated for input sequences, but this will be used as the input for automatically reversed rules

items.description: A namespaced ID pointing to a block group (e.g. 'builtin:cyrillic-letters')
